diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: After public protests supporting Milad Armoon and Navid Najaran and the suspension of their death sentences, many citizens reacted to the wave of executions in Iran by sending messages to Iran International's media outlets. Responding to a message attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei about the necessity of childbearing, the audience pointed to the killing, blinding, flogging, and repression of their children, highlighting the contradiction between this request and the government's behavior towards the people.

Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund fans honored the memory of Iranian fans Aref Jafarzadeh and Sarina Esmaeilzadeh, who were killed during protests against the Islamic Republic, with a banner at the Emirates Stadium in London during their Champions League match. This took place on November 24. Aref Jafarzadeh died in December 1404 and Sarina Esmaeilzadeh in 1401 during protests.

On the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, combating gender-based violence has become a key issue in Spain's electoral competitions and political debates. Various parties have proposed programs to support victims and increase penalties for perpetrators. Sadaf Baghbani, an Iran International reporter, has reported.

Amirhossein Bankipour, a member of the Parliamentary Cultural Commission, proposed three solutions—marriage, chastity, and long-term engagement—to address the sexual needs of young people. He said only 1% of boys and 20% of girls under 20 get married, and young people face peak sexual needs alongside extensive online stimuli. His third solution is long-term engagement, where couples can remain engaged for several years until conditions for shared life are met.

Mohammad Akraminia, spokesperson for the Islamic Republic Army, announced that vessels must coordinate with the Islamic Republic Armed Forces for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz. He said that the level of surveillance over this waterway has increased with the deployment of new systems and stricter control is being applied. He also stated that vessels passing without coordination have faced greater risks and have encountered mines.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said Trump seeks to gain maximum concessions from the Islamic Republic at minimal cost and emphasized that the statements of Islamic Republic military officials about breaking the US naval blockade are more like boasting. He added that Tehran is currently seeking to overcome economic pressures, not to engage in a broad military confrontation with the US.

Hossein Samsami, Tehran representative in parliament, said in a virtual parliamentary session on Wednesday, 4 Azar, that both the Central Bank and the government are playing on the enemy's field, as the Central Bank increases the exchange rate daily. He added that the rise in exchange rates and leaving imports and pricing to the free market creates demand for currency.

Aram News, citing informed sources in the White House and CIA, reported that the Islamic Republic has sought North Korean expertise to develop missile launch pads. This cooperation was remote, and sanctions have hindered Tehran's missile capability restoration goals. Estimates indicate Iran has only restored about 40% of its pre-recent war missile capacity.

The Economist reported on the expansion of economic and military cooperation between China, Russia, the Islamic Republic, and North Korea in what it called the "quadruple axis of evil." According to the report, China buys oil from Iran and Russia, the Islamic Republic provides drones and missiles to Russia, and North Korea supplies ammunition and military equipment to Moscow. Russia shares its military technology and experience with these countries.

Mohammad Dadkan, former head of the Football Federation, said in the online program 'Tak Be Tak' that IRIB is the biggest center of lies in the country and he refused to appear there. He also criticized those who talk about religion but behave differently. Dadkan asked if he would be considered anti-religion and anti-revolution for saying these things.

The Ministry of Science of the Islamic Republic stated that students who planned and caused riots will not be allowed to return to university. Masoud Pezeshkian said he prevented a decision to bar 2,000 students from entering universities. The Ministry considers the flag of the Islamic Republic and Ali Khamenei as definite red lines and said educational measures for remorseful students do not mean ignoring legal actions against violators.

Hassan Qashqavi, spokesperson for the National Security Commission of the Parliament, stated that the Islamic Republic "is still in a state of war and the clashes continue." He said fighters are being killed and that there is no "hardliner or moderate" faction in the Islamic Republic's structure, with the final decision made by Mojtaba Khamenei.

The Deputy of Treatment at the Ministry of Health reported that from 10 Aban to 3 Azar, 356 people in various cities across the country suffered poisoning from alcohol consumption and 20 people died. The highest number of cases was reported in Nishapur with 211 cases. Additionally, 80 people underwent dialysis and 33 are hospitalized in intensive care units.

A worker sent a video to Iran International reporting a gas outage in a brick kiln and said the lack of gas in cold weather has disrupted work. He opened the stove valve without flame and said, "We are seasonal workers, we came here but there is no gas to work in this cold."

On the evening of Sunday, 1 Azar, the home of Nakisa Moradipour and Shayan Maneshadi, a Baháʼí couple in Kerman, was searched by security forces. Officers entered the home without a judicial warrant and confiscated four mobile phones, two laptops, one iPad, and the guests' mobile phones. The guests' cars were also searched by security forces.

The price of the dollar in Tehran's free market rose to a historic record of 288,000 tomans amid intensified sanctions and a crisis in settling the government's foreign currency debts. Nearly a thousand companies have been waiting for about 20 months to receive their foreign currency claims. Essential goods importers protested for two consecutive days in front of the Ministries of Agriculture Jihad and Economy against this situation.

Zohreh Lajvardi, a Tehran representative in parliament, said about the 14-year delay of the women's protection bill that their definition of violence is completely different from the Western perspective. She added that there should be an explanation for the insistence on using the term violence and asked if they intend to act according to the 2030 documents. Lajvardi also said Islam defends women's rights more than any other religion and this is provable.

Zahra Behrouz Azar, Vice President for Women and Family Affairs, stated that the government has so far been unable to establish a clear supervisory mechanism to address the problems of women working in private and contract companies. Some pregnant women face termination and referral to unemployment insurance instead of maternity leave. This situation is more difficult for women working in workshops without insurance coverage and may deprive them of rights related to pregnancy, maternity leave, and social security support.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said Trump has effectively opened the way for Israel to test the regime change option. He also noted that increased military pressure by Riyadh and support from its allies could force the Houthis to retreat.

The family of Rasoul Ziaei Zardkhoshoui, killed in the protests on 18 Dey in Fooladshahr, Isfahan, have been repeatedly pressured by the IRGC to accept the official narrative about how he was killed. Agents had demanded 2 billion tomans from his family for the delivery of his body.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, said he did not turn off any light but did not turn on extra lights and considers himself obliged to prevent excessive resource consumption. He added that to reach the peak, hardships must be endured and he will prevent wastefulness, whether mocked or not. Pezeshkian does not believe that the presidency grants permission for wastefulness.

Iraqi media reported the relocation of proxy forces of the Islamic Republic in the country and the rebuilding of their forces. Al-Mada newspaper reported that these groups are strengthening their military positions in anticipation of a possible resumption of war between Iran and the United States.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin, a member of the Iran International editorial team, said that if the Iraqi government cannot eliminate the proxy forces of the Islamic Republic in the country, Iraq will also be destroyed. He added that the Islamic Republic has destroyed Iran and Lebanon and wants to drag everyone into fire with it. According to him, the Iraqi government must succeed in this matter.

A member of the board of the Construction Workers' Trade Associations said that in the past four to five years, about 300,000 to 400,000 construction workers have been waiting for insurance, and only half of the promised quota of 10,000 has been allocated so far. Akbar Shokat criticized the new Social Security Organization directive and reported that insurance for workers with other business licenses is at risk of being cut, with a list of 400 workers prepared in one Social Security branch in Qom province. He also mentioned problems such as non-payment of insurance premiums for six months, temporary employment abroad, and repeated inspections threatening the insurance security of these workers.

Raheem Sterling, former England national football player, was sentenced to 12 months suspended imprisonment for dangerous driving, refusing to provide a sample to police, and possession of nitrous oxide. He was also banned from driving for two years and sentenced to 100 hours of community service. The sentence followed his arrest in May near the M3 motorway.
A teenage girl in Mashhad who intended to commit suicide was saved from death by the intervention of police officers and a police station social worker.

Babak Moradifar, a political activist, was transferred to Greater Tehran Prison after referring to the prosecutor's office to serve his 30-month prison sentence. This news was reported by Harana News Agency. He informed about his transfer to the second hall of Ward Six in this prison on 3 Azar.

The US government is preparing new tariffs against the European Union, China, and several other countries. The White House stated that the reason for this decision is the protective policies of America's trade partners. These policies have caused a flood of cheap goods into the US.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International reporting that at 7 a.m., a fuel station in Boumehen was selling gasoline only with fuel cards and announced to vehicles without cards that gasoline was not available.

The imminent execution sentences of Milad Armoon and Navid Najaran have sparked waves of anger, sorrow, and calls to stop the executions on social media. Ayah Dris, a member of Iran International's editorial team, speaks about these reactions.

Bianca Mainl Reisinger, Austria's Foreign Minister, called the flogging sentence of Parasto Ahmadi and four others torture and a violation of international law. She emphasized that the Islamic Republic fears independent women and supported the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights' call to abolish flogging in Iran. Mainl Reisinger stated Austria stands with Iranian women and will advocate for their rights at the UN Security Council.

The Conversation reported that the experimental drug "Diranersen" has been able to slow the decline of memory and cognitive abilities in Alzheimer's patients by up to 54% in a clinical trial. This drug works by reducing the production of the protein "Tau" in brain cells, unlike approved drugs that focus on clearing amyloid protein. Current approved drugs may have significant side effects, but Diranersen reduces Tau protein production from the start.

On Tuesday, 3 Azar, groups of migrants arrived by boat from the coasts of Africa to the island of El Hierro in Spain, and maritime rescue forces assisted them. These arrivals are part of a wave of migration to the Canary Islands via the dangerous Atlantic Ocean route. Local authorities declared a state of emergency due to the arrival of several thousand migrants to this island.
Videos received by Iran International from Bushehr show the presence of armed agents of the Islamic Republic and the creation of a severe security atmosphere on Wednesday, the fourth of Azar.

Five media outlets in Ilam were suspended by order of the provincial prosecutor. The suspensions followed the publication of critical content regarding the performance of the governor of Ilam, especially related to a deadly bus accident.

Harana news agency reported that Garanaz Mousavi, a poet and filmmaker, was summoned to the criminal enforcement branch of Tehran's Culture and Media Prosecutor's Office to serve a prison sentence under electronic monitoring. The summons was issued on Tuesday, Azar 3, and Mousavi must appear within five days to serve the sentence. The conviction relates to a case from 1390 concerning the making of the film "My Tehran, Auction."

Bayern Munich issued an official statement after Karl-Heinz Rummenigge's controversial remarks about Jamal Musiala's health and salary, expressing full support for the young star. Rummenigge had said that Musiala's return to his previous level is difficult and his contract figures are no longer justifiable. Max Eberl held a meeting with Musiala's representatives, and both sides agreed to continue negotiations in a confidential and friendly atmosphere.
Due to rising concerns about possible drone attacks on British military bases, the UK's Air Force has increased protective measures for its military aircraft.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, on Wednesday, 4 Azar, likened the Islamic Republic to a sinking ship in a message on the social network X, saying that Iran no longer has even a drop of oil on the water to sell. Bessent added that since the start of the US Treasury's "economic isolation" operation in August, Iran has not been able to load even one oil tanker.

A video shows a group of 115 emergency staff in Kermanshah gathered in front of the governor's office on the 3rd of Azar, demanding the removal of injustice in the payment of tariffs and bonuses for medical emergencies and transparency in the payment process.
The Deputy of Primary Education at the Kurdistan Department of Education reported the identification of 1,695 children who have dropped out of school in this province.

An image of the grave of Majid Nikandish, a detainee from the January protests whose death sentence was carried out on 8 Mehr 1405 in Mashhad, has been published. His body was not handed over to his family and was buried in Behesht Reza Cemetery by order of the Mashhad prosecutor. Nikandish was arrested on charges of "enmity against God" and sentenced to death, and his execution was carried out simultaneously with Ali Hemmati Sistani.

Zohreh Lajvardi, Tehran representative, said about the 14-year delay of the women's protection bill that the definition of violence in this bill differs from the Western perspective and the term violence should not be used in a way that Westerners can make demands from Iran. Masoud Pezeshkian, the Islamic Republic's president, on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, stated that the Prophet of Islam was a flagbearer against violence towards women and that laws must ensure women's rights and security. However, women's situation in Iran still faces extensive legal and social restrictions.

Amirhossein Hosseinzadeh, Tractor's star, after injury in the match against Al Wasl UAE and rumors about a torn knee ligament, announced on Instagram that he has no problem continuing the season. Tractor's doctor also denied the possibility of a torn ligament and said initial MRI examinations showed no signs of severe injury.

Valerie Hayer, French representative in the European Parliament and head of the 'New Europe' political group, condemned the flogging sentence of Parasto Ahmadi and declared strong support for Iranian women fighting for freedom. She emphasized that the rights of Iranian women are non-negotiable and no woman should be beaten for her choice of clothing or punished for raising her voice. Hayer added that freedom means having the right to sing, speak, and walk in the street without fear.

Majid Bahiraei, one of the detainees of the national revolution in Nahavand, said in a message from prison about the November 17 protests of the people of Abdanan that people shouted the name of Prince Reza Pahlavi in the streets. He added that one can criticize the prince or consider another form of government, but the voice of the people should not be denied.

Ali Pourdarab, a journalist residing in Kermanshah, was sentenced by the Revolutionary Court of that city to one year in prison, two years of travel ban, and two years of professional ban in journalism. The sentence was issued on charges of propaganda against the regime. This information was reported by the HRANA news agency.

Ahmad Taheri, head of the National Center for Air and Climate Change of the Environmental Protection Organization, announced that according to Ministry of Health studies, 58,975 people die annually in the country due to air pollution. He said Ahvaz, with 247 unhealthy days, remains the most polluted city, and the number of unhealthy days in Mashhad and Tehran in 1404 has increased by 57% compared to 1400. Taheri also emphasized the aging transportation fleet and delays in implementing some renovation plans as factors contributing to ongoing air pollution.

The Union of Truck Drivers' Associations has reported the continuation of the drivers' strike for the fourth day. Reza Akbari, head of the Road Maintenance Organization, denied the strike on Monday and said that road transport fleet operations are normal. Mehdi Beigi, a member of Iran International's editorial team, examines the income and expenses of truck drivers and the reasons for their protests in "Peyvast".

While the dollar price in Tehran exceeded 292,000 tomans, Trump announced funding for the war with the Islamic Republic until the end of January. The Israeli defense minister said the country would prevent Tehran from acquiring chemical weapons through attacks. At the same time, Rezaei said the armed forces would break the siege.
A video shows a group of schoolgirls singing the song "Nam-e Javid-e Vatan" at Persepolis.
A worker at Sungun copper mine lost his life. It was reported that one of the employees of the Ahan-Ajin contracting company died due to an accident while working at the Sungun copper mine.

The global campaign "Orange the World" has released a report on violence against women in Iran over the past year, coinciding with November 25, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. According to the data, at least 104 cases of women being killed, 178 cases of domestic violence, and 63 cases of sexual assault and harassment have been documented. Additionally, over 13,000 examinations of women claiming physical spousal abuse were reported in the first quarter of the current year.

A video sent to Iran International shows the decorated grave of Mohammadreza Askari Mohammadi on his birthday. This 18-year-old protester was shot and killed on 18 Dey 1404 near the Moshirieh police station in Tehran.

Agence France-Presse reported on Wednesday, quoting a judicial official, that a Lebanese judge issued an official arrest warrant for five Hezbollah members previously detained in northern Lebanon and ordered three other members to be handed over for interrogation. These individuals were arrested in a mountainous area between Batroun and Bsharri and face charges including forming an armed group and supplying weapons.

Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, President of Egypt, emphasized the importance of ensuring freedom and security of navigation in international waterways during a meeting with Vincent Clerc, CEO of Maersk, on Wednesday, 4 Azar. El-Sisi stated that Egypt will continue its efforts to reduce tensions and maintain freedom of navigation. The Maersk CEO said the company has resumed operations through the Suez Canal and the Red Sea and will fully restore its shipping network to this route in the coming months.

The Yemeni government reported that Hezbollah has started operations to transfer its resources and activities to Yemen. According to the report, the Houthis supported by the Islamic Republic are establishing a network across the region and the Red Sea in cooperation with the Al-Shabaab movement in Somalia.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing severe air pollution in Abadan on the 4th of Azar and criticized the schools not being closed despite these conditions.

Hamidreza Moghaddamfar, advisor to the commander of the IRGC, said that if another war occurs, the geographical scope of the Islamic Republic's response will extend beyond the region and its military doctrine will change. He also stated that Iran has gone through two wars with these parties and they were defeated in both and did not achieve their goals.

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, rejected Israel's claims about the production and concealment of chemical weapons in Iran's pharmaceutical factories and accused Israel of trying to drag the US into another war with the Islamic Republic. Araghchi said Israel has refused to join international conventions banning nuclear, chemical, and biological weapons and possesses hundreds of nuclear warheads. He also referred to Iran's membership in the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and the Chemical Weapons Convention, stating that Iran itself was a victim of chemical weapons supplied by West Germany to Saddam Hussein's regime.

Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition, reported on Wednesday, 4 Azar, that a projectile fired by the Houthis hit the Jazan port in southern Saudi Arabia. Al-Maliki stated that the attack caused minor damage, but no civilians were harmed. He added that efforts to determine the type of projectile fired by the Houthis are ongoing.

Mehrdad Khazaei-Pool, director general of natural resources and watershed management of Mazandaran - Nowshahr, reported a fire in the forested heights of Kajur district. The fire was reported around 18:00 local time in the Farakh area, and six firefighting teams were dispatched to the site. Difficult access and darkness have complicated fire containment operations.

On the evening of Saturday, 30 Aban, Soroush Gilani was arrested in Abdanan by intelligence forces and transferred to an unknown location. The number of detainees related to the protest gathering on 26 Aban in this county reached at least 19 people.

The public and revolutionary prosecutor of Ardabil province reported the arrest of a social media activist for publishing content on one of the social networks. The citizen is accused of "insulting the sacred."

Abdolnaser Hemmati, the governor of the Central Bank of the Islamic Republic, said that the currency market has had relative stability in the past two months due to the Central Bank's measures. He attributed the increase in the dollar rate to US sanctions on the Iran Currency and Gold Exchange Center and accusations regarding the Islamic Republic's shadow banking network. Hemmati also accused media linked to the US and Israel of creating a negative atmosphere about Iran's currency market.

Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel, on Wednesday, 4 Azar, in response to the preliminary approval of a bill concerning candidates under judicial prosecution in the country's parliament, accused his political rivals of trying to disqualify him and said such actions happen in Iran. He also called on all Israeli citizens to strive for reconciliation and unity and added that they must unite to face immediate dangers.

It was reported that Danial Habibollahi, a law graduate, was arrested and transferred to prison on Sunday, 1 Azar, to serve his prison sentence. He had previously been sentenced by a judicial authority to three years of retributive imprisonment and four years of suspended imprisonment.

A report on the latest status of Morad Mohammadi, a political prisoner serving his sentence in Ilam prison, has been published. He was previously sentenced to more than four years in prison by the Revolutionary Court.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing a receipt for a carton of eggs priced at 680,000 tomans and criticized Masoud Pezeshkian for inflation, power and water outages, and gas shortages, saying: "What kind of power is this that every day we return to the Stone Age?"

The Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera reported that in addition to two Russian ships targeted in drone attacks by Ukraine at the port of Benghazi, Libya, an Iranian cargo ship named "Alvan," likely carrying electronic parts used in drone battles, was also attacked. The ship was hit by a drone but did not sink and was moved to a dock at the port. Unlike the attacks on Russian ships, no party has claimed responsibility for the attack on the Iranian ship.
Niusha Saremi reported in Titrawal that tensions have escalated from Hormuz to the Red Sea. It was also reported that suspicious underground facilities have been constructed in Bahjatabad.

Masoud Bidarigh, a former political prisoner, told Iran International that Rasht turned into a battlefield on January 8 and 9, with security forces shooting at unarmed protesters. He witnessed security forces shooting at a young man near Somayeh Park and said people came to the streets empty-handed.

The global campaign "16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence" takes place annually from November 25 to December 10. The campaign emphasizes the link between fighting violence against women and defending human rights. Violence against women is one of the most widespread human rights violations rooted in power inequality and discrimination.

Satellite images indicate the construction of a fortified underground complex near Bahjatabad. The purpose of these facilities is not yet clear, but missile, military, or nuclear activities have been suggested.

Na'im Qasim, Secretary-General of Hezbollah Lebanon, on Wednesday, 4 Azar, emphasized the necessity of maintaining the group's unity with the Islamic Republic, saying that Iran works for Hezbollah and bears the burdens of problems on their behalf. He added that after the failure of the framework agreement, the Islamic Republic stopped the attacks within the current limits. Qasim also accused the US of pressuring Lebanese officials to make concessions to Israel.

At least two protest gatherings were held today, Wednesday, 4 Azar. Some people and families of political prisoners gathered in front of Qezel Hesar prison in Karaj to protest the death sentences of Milad Armoon and Navid Najaran. Also, a group of retired employees of Homa Airlines held a protest in front of the Ministry of Roads and Urban Development building in Tehran.
On the afternoon of Wednesday, 4 Azar, a worker at the Ashkali Hajdak coal mine in the Kohsaran district of Ravar county died due to a fall from height.

In the AFC Champions League 2 match between Al Jazira and Gol Gohar, the Syrian referee was replaced at halftime due to suspicion of alcohol consumption. Gol Gohar's manager stated the referee was acting abnormally and their team refused to continue playing until the referee was replaced following their threat. Gol Gohar lost the match 1-0 and was eliminated from the competition.

A video released on social media shows that the fourth anniversary of the martyrdom of Mehran Basir Tavana was commemorated with the presence of justice-seeking families at his grave. Mehran, 29 years old and from Fuman, was killed by suppressors' gunfire in Aban 1401 during the "Woman, Life, Freedom" uprising in Somesara while helping an injured woman.

Gabriel Attal, a candidate in the French presidential election, condemned the execution of the 74 lashes sentence against Parasto Ahmadi for performing a concert without a hijab. He wrote on Instagram that the mullahs have prisons and paramilitary forces but tremble before a young woman and a microphone. Attal also expressed solidarity with the people of Iran, saying that one day Iran will sing freely and live freely.
On Wednesday, 4 Azar, Mahdi Mahmoudian, a civil activist, was arrested by security forces at his home and transferred to an unknown location.

The death sentence of a defendant in Tehran was overturned by the Supreme Court, and his case was referred back to the Criminal Court One of Tehran Province for reconsideration. Additionally, four prisoners sentenced to death in Kouhdasht, Sanandaj, and Maragheh were released from the gallows after the forgiveness of the victims' families.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said on the program "Cheshmandaz" that Iranian women, despite their leading role in social changes over the past three decades, still face government and domestic violence. He emphasized that both the government and part of society play a role in reproducing this violence.
A resident of Chatab village in Miyaneh county told Iran International in a video that the electricity in their village is cut off several times a day and each time for several hours.

Houthi forces supported by the Islamic Republic announced on Wednesday, 4 Azar, that they attacked the ports of Jeddah and Jazan in Saudi Arabia. Yahya Saree, the military spokesman for the Houthis, said the group will continue its military operations deep inside Saudi Arabia. The military spokesman warned that the group will not hesitate to respond immediately to any Saudi attack on the port of Hodeidah.

Yousef Memar, Ali-Asghar Baghjeri, and Morteza Baghjeri have been held in indefinite detention in Sabzevar prison for over six months. These three individuals were arrested in connection with the nationwide protests of Dey 1404. Additionally, Javad Ghazimanesh and Javad Saadatifar, who were arrested simultaneously, have been released on bail.

New satellite images show that the Islamic Republic is rapidly constructing a fortified underground complex near Bahjatabad, between the two nuclear centers of Isfahan and Natanz. The Institute for Science and International Security reports that construction began about a year ago and its progress speed is unusual. Analysts have suggested possible missile or other military use, and nuclear use has not been ruled out.
A citizen showed in a video sent to Iran International the emission of smoke from the Chenaran sugar factory on the 4th of Azar and said that this factory is burning mazut.

On November 25, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, while news of femicide continues to emerge from Iran, some Iran International audience members shared their untold experiences of years of sexual harassment, rape, domestic violence, forced marriage, child marriage, and gender discrimination. These accounts indicate the widespread violence against women at home, school, street, and workplace. Many women said fear of judgment, threats, and lack of legal support forced them into years of silence.

The Institute for Science and International Security reported satellite images showing rapid construction of fortified underground facilities in Bahjatabad. The institute stated that extensive security measures indicate a possible military use of the facilities and did not rule out a connection to the Islamic Republic's nuclear program. The complex is about 49 square kilometers, with initial construction signs identified in early December 2025.
A report has been presented about the hidden complicity of a part of society with the government in suppressing women.

Jonathan Schaech, an analyst at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, said that after the failure of negotiations and unsuccessful efforts to change the behavior of the Islamic Republic, there are more serious signs of Washington's desire to change the government in Iran. He added that Tehran is also preparing for a new round of conflict by moving military infrastructure underground and preparing government forces.

A video released on social media shows a memorial birthday ceremony held at the grave of Artin Khajavi. Artin Khajavi-Nia, a 16-year-old student, was shot dead on 18 Dey 1404 [Gregorian: 2027-01-08] in front of the Qods city governor's office.

Prince Reza Pahlavi, appreciating the condemnation of Parasto Ahmadi's flogging by international officials and media, called this crime the tip of the iceberg. He referred to the situation of other political prisoners, including Milad Armoon and Navid Najaran, who face execution. Pahlavi called for practical action by the world to stop these crimes against humanity.

Jamshid Barzegar, a journalist and political analyst, said that the continuation of the US naval blockade and increased economic pressure have put the Islamic Republic in a difficult position. According to him, Tehran may resort to offensive operations and increased tensions in the region to get out of this situation.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International saying that the shampoo he bought last month for 430,000 tomans is now priced at 698,000 tomans, and he criticized the government's response to people's protests.

Ali Sadzadeh said that Houthi attacks on economic and infrastructure targets in Saudi Arabia and the escalation of clashes in Bab al-Mandab have posed a serious challenge to Riyadh. He added that the lack of cohesion among Yemen government forces and the inability of airstrikes to contain the Houthis have put Saudi Arabia in a deadlock. Sadzadeh also linked the developments in Yemen to tensions in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz.

Ahmad Bakhshayesh Ardestani, a member of the National Security and Foreign Policy Commission, said the Islamic Republic should respond to Ukraine's attacks on Iranian ships. He added that representatives of Iran, China, and Russia are coming together to form a union for military, intelligence, and technological cooperation. Bakhshayesh Ardestani also said Yahya Rahim Safavi's trip to Russia is for decision-making, not arms purchases, and noted that Russia and China have changed their outlook under new conditions.

Reuters reported, citing an eyewitness, hearing several explosions in Riyadh. A Saudi-led coalition announced that it intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by Yemeni Houthis towards Riyadh. Saudi civil defense warned of a potential danger in Riyadh and later announced that the danger was removed.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, said the president who was supposed to create openings has now reached a point where he wishes for death. He pointed out that while oil exports have stopped, ports are under siege, and the dollar has reached 300,000 tomans, Pezeshkian calls for an agreement and IRGC commanders chant for expanding the war. He added that Pezeshkian's wish for death is a sign of the president's despair and the intensification of the rift at the top of the Islamic Republic's governance.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said the dollar has reached the threshold of 300,000 tomans with its continued price surge. He added that the currency market is reacting to the fading likelihood of an agreement, increased risk of war, cut in oil revenues, and severe budget deficit. Also, Scott Bassett, the US Treasury Secretary, likened the Islamic Republic's economy to a sinking ship.

Hossein Taeb, head of the Basij Organization, said the Islamic Republic will not rest until it takes revenge for the killed, including Ali Khamenei, students of Minab school, scientists, women, and men. He added that "criminal and arrogant rulers" will have a fate similar to Saddam.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said: "Today, not only the people of Iran but also the US, Europe, and Arab countries face a choice; to support the Iranian people in the path of overthrowing the Islamic Republic or to accept the risk of the emergence of a regime equipped with nuclear, chemical, and biological weapons, intercontinental missiles, and dirty bombs; a threat that could endanger the security of all these countries."

Videos released on social media show a large fire on the afternoon of Wednesday, 4 Azar in Cairo. The Egyptian Ministry of Health announced that following the overturning of a fuel tanker on the Cairo Ring Road, at least 30 people were killed and 19 injured. Egyptian authorities have started investigations into the cause of the incident.

Paris Saint-Germain football team was held to a 2-2 draw at home against Roma in the fifth week of the UEFA Champions League, losing points for the first time this season. Mario Hermoso scored for Roma in the 5th minute and Ilia Zabarnyi equalized in the 31st minute. Ousmane Dembélé put Paris Saint-Germain ahead in the 62nd minute, but Donyell Malen scored Roma's equalizer in the 78th minute.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported early Thursday receiving a report of an explosion caused by an unidentified projectile near an oil tanker 50 nautical miles west of Dubai in the UAE. The tanker commander reported the explosion, but no damage was caused to the vessel and there were no environmental consequences. All crew members are safe and their status has been confirmed.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, said that the Iranian regime is a sinking ship and since the US Treasury started the "economic expulsion" operation in August, Iran has not been able to load even one oil tanker and now has not a single drop of oil on the water for sale.

BBC Sport reported that David Cook, head of the independent body overseeing English football, told Parliament that the body is ready to act against Manchester City if the club's conviction for breaching Premier League financial rules is confirmed. The body has the authority to remove unqualified directors and even force owners to sell the club. Cook emphasized that evidence and legal requirements, not political considerations or the club's size, will be the criteria for decision-making.

Ben Sabti, a researcher on Iran and Israel issues in Tel Aviv, talks about the coalition agreement between the Yashar party led by Gadi Eisenkot and the Our Home Israel party, the probable composition of the future government, and the implications of this coalition on Israel's political equations.

The office of Prince Reza Pahlavi expressed concern that establishing a Basij military training base near Persepolis, one of Iran's registered World Heritage sites, endangers it. The office emphasized that no military entity has the right to jeopardize the security of this ancient site for its own purposes. It added that Persepolis does not belong to any specific government or generation, and protecting it means safeguarding Iran's history and preserving a heritage that must be passed on to future generations.

North Korea's official news agency reported that Kim Jong Un emphasized the need to deploy tactical nuclear weapons during a visit to nuclear facilities and announced a systematic increase in nuclear material production capacity. He stated that North Korea's status as a nuclear-armed country is inviolable and any attempt to deny this status would be considered a "declaration of war." Hours after these remarks, South Korea's Ministry of Defense said North Korea must stop justifying its nuclear program and comply with UN Security Council resolutions.

Al Hadath network reported, citing informed sources, that Khaled Abunda, a Hamas commander, and his wife were killed after their apartment in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza Strip was targeted. Earlier, the Israeli army and Shin Bet had announced targeting a senior Hamas member in the Gaza Strip.

The Global Campaign for Solidarity Against Gender Apartheid stated on the occasion of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women that 85 cases of women and girls being killed in Iran have been recorded in the past three months. The campaign demanded the criminalization of gender apartheid and an end to impunity for perpetrators of violence. A human rights site also reported that in the past year, at least 104 cases of femicide, 178 cases of domestic violence, and 63 cases of sexual assault and harassment against women in Iran have been documented.

Alison Hooker, the US Deputy Political Secretary of State, referred to her meeting with leaders of the Gulf Cooperation Council member countries and Jordan, stating that coordinated actions in the Strait of Hormuz and within the framework of economic isolation operations increase pressure on the Islamic Republic, and the results are becoming apparent. She also said that in the meeting with leaders of the Gulf Cooperation Council member countries and Jordan, they discussed regional security and efforts to increase pressure on the Islamic Republic.

A Western diplomatic source told Israel Hayom that Western countries' intelligence indicates the Islamic Republic has tried for several decades to develop chemical weapons. However, there is no evidence that Tehran has obtained such weapons.

The Institute for Science and International Security reported the rapid construction of a fortified underground facility in the Bahjatabad area, between Natanz and Isfahan, based on satellite images. According to the report, construction began in Azar of last year and has continued at an unusual speed in recent months.

Canada's Security Intelligence Service announced it has started direct and extensive talks with the Iranian and Jewish communities in the country to counter transnational repression and foreign interference. The director general of the strategic office of this service said the goal of these meetings is to build trust, hear threats directly, and share security information with citizens.

Erfan Ghanei-Fard, a security studies researcher, said the Islamic Republic needs to reproduce an imaginary enemy and create crises to suppress internally and maintain power. He added that in the Khomeinist ideological system, war is a tool to legitimize the rulers' power and sustain the government.

Farzin Nadimi, a senior defense and security researcher, said the newly constructed underground tunnels in Isfahan are likely related to the Islamic Republic's missile program and are used for storing and housing missiles.

Ghassan Ashour, a Middle East analyst, said that smuggling oil, currency, and goods through Iraq is carried out with the participation of some officials and political actors in Baghdad and the Kurdistan Region. He added that part of the revenues from these transactions goes to the Islamic Republic and the Revolutionary Guards and is used to finance Tehran-affiliated militias in the region.

The Financial Times reported the role of the IRGC's secret cyber unit called "Martyr Kaveh Unit" in attacking the cooling systems of hundreds of stores in France. According to the report, this unit has previously been involved in cyberattacks on US industrial infrastructure.

Al Hadath network reported, citing American sources, that Hezbollah has regained 50 percent of its capabilities and power. According to these American sources, Washington is trying to hold a political meeting between Lebanon and Israel within the next two or three weeks.

The White House announced that Donald Trump and Mark Rutte discussed conflicts in Iran and the Russia-Ukraine war during a meeting at Mar-a-Lago. Investment in defense and efforts to end the Ukraine war were other topics of discussion. Trump had previously criticized European allies for insufficient support and defense spending.

In the match between Gol Gohar Sirjan and Al Jazira in the AFC Champions League, the Syrian referee was replaced by the fourth official at halftime after controversial decisions and player protests. Gol Gohar's manager stated the referee was not in a normal state and the club warned that players would not return to the field if the referee was not replaced. The Asian Football Confederation has not yet provided an official explanation for the referee's replacement.

Fararu news agency reported that at the start of trading on Thursday, 5 Azar, the dollar rate reached 292,890. The price of the US dollar in Tehran's free market set a new record on Wednesday, 4 Azar, reaching 290,500 tomans in Tehran's Ferdowsi market.

Hamidreza Hajibabaei, the Deputy Speaker of the Parliament, stated that the only way to confront the US is "siege against siege" and threatened that if Iran's oil is not exported, no oil will leave the region. He added that if regional countries assist the US, the Islamic Republic will target the entire area. He also mentioned the possibility of changing the Islamic Republic's defense doctrine if necessary.

Islamabad hosts a meeting of senior political, defense, and military officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey to discuss practical steps for implementing the joint defense pact of Mecca. This meeting is held after the official enforcement of the pact and amid increasing concerns about regional threats. Javad Hamdani, a reporter from Iran International, reports.

Esteghlal team became the women's ice hockey premier league champion by defeating the Penguins 4-1, four weeks before the end of the competition. Yeganeh Bahrami leads the scorers table with 12 goals, and Hadiseh Pourhashami follows her teammate with 11 goals.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International saying that on 5 Azar, due to a power outage in Tehran, the elevator stopped and he has to wait about two hours until the power is restored.

Israel Katz, Israel's Defense Minister, announced that if Hamas does not disarm voluntarily, the Israeli army will launch a new military operation in the Gaza Strip. He said Hamas must disarm voluntarily or the Israeli army will do so. Katz added that Hamas's control over the remaining 30% of the Gaza Strip is an illusion and the army will continue efforts to end Hamas.

LeBron James, 41, shined with his first triple-double for the Philadelphia 76ers in the absence of key stars, scoring 25 points, 12 assists, and 10 rebounds in a 111-104 win over the Miami Heat. This was James's sixth triple-double after turning 40, a rare feat in NBA history. He had standout moments in the second and fourth quarters.

Houshang Hasenyari, an expert on Middle East and military affairs, said the Islamic Republic uses all available capacities to acquire unconventional weapons, including nuclear and chemical weapons. He stated that if the Islamic Republic obtains these weapons, given the regime's anti-Israeli policies, the possibility of using them against Israel can be considered.

Israeli media reported a tense phone call between Benjamin Netanyahu and Donald Trump regarding military action against the Islamic Republic. According to informed sources, Netanyahu tried to convince Trump to carry out a military attack in the near future during this call.

Mohammad Zouri, one of those arrested in connection with the protests of Dey 1404, remains in detention in Damghan prison without a clear status despite about six months having passed since his arrest.

Reza Shasipour was killed on 18 Dey during popular protests in the city of Izeh by direct gunfire from the Islamic Republic's suppression forces. His name remains in the memory of this land and his memory is a guiding light for freedom seekers.

A shopkeeper sent a video to Iran International saying that on the 5th of Azar, the electricity of a production workshop in Yaftabad, Tehran, was cut off from 9 AM and will not be restored until 12 PM. In reaction to this situation, he said: "I remember Khamenei's famous phrase that Islam is exactly this; not one word less, not one word more."

Hana Hattab, the Syrian referee of the Gol Gohar and Al Jazira match, reacted to accusations of alcohol consumption and his sudden substitution at halftime, threatening critics with official complaints and legal action. He expressed strong complaints about privacy invasion in a message on his personal page and stated that he will pursue any insults and defamation through judicial authorities. Hana Hattab also mentioned that before issuing an official statement about the AFC Champions League 2 events, he is waiting for the Syrian Football Federation's stance.

Mohammad Reza Aref, the First Vice President, expressed surprise at the increase in the price of macaroni and called for a reduction in prices. He said, "For once, make the people happy, lower the prices, and we will pray for you."
